chapter_note: The chapter contains a substantial enumerative teaching core (seven benefits of the Sun; seven evils of the Night; five archetypes; three further archetypes corresponding to the mystery of the Father). It is wrapped in a hagiographic dialogue frame and repeatedly interrupted by editorial application/polemic against “the sects” and by a late Christian overlay at the end (a ‘saviour’ saying; ‘children of the day/light’). The second-half application drift matches the fatigue signal: the cosmological-cosmological correspondences remain, but are increasingly turned into exhortation and sectarian contrast.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic opening scene with ‘the apostle’ seated among disciples; hagiographic narrative container rather than systematic teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: it is the gate of life and the vessel of peace, to this great aeon of light [...].
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue tag (“He says,”) as frame attribution; removed the anti-OT/‘Satan’ law polemic and paraphrased legal threat (“Whoever will worship it can die…”) because it maps the Sun’s mystery onto a historical law/institutional prohibition (cosmos→contemporary religious landscape).
paragraphs.temporal_note: First clause is a cosmological definition (Sun as ‘gate/vessel’ within the aeon). The remainder pivots into editorial polemic anchored in ‘his law’ (Deuteronomy tradition) and worship-prohibition.
Application/polemic register (‘people are blind… even today’), addressing contemporary ignorance rather than expounding the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: Every day, would this great light-giver shine its light, it shall do seven good things for them. Shall they not see them?
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumerative structuring move (‘seven good things’) introducing a systematic list; largely impersonal despite rhetorical question.

paragraphs.core_text: The first good thing that it does for them is its light, which it shines upon them. It opens the eyes of all mankind. They see underfoot as they walk by it. It takes away the blindness of the night, which made them blind with its darkness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered, impersonal exposition of a fixed set (1/7); operates as day/night correspondence without institutional anchoring.

paragraphs.core_text: The second: When (the Sun) is come to the world, with its coming it shall bring calm and peace to the entire world. With its coming it shall also take away from them all the fear and trembling, which their heart is filled with the whole night; for it shall take away the darkness present by its light, and sweep it out. Also, this is how it extinguishes fear by its calm.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered correspondential effect-list (2/7), describing mechanism (light dispels darkness/fear) rather than exhorting.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is its vigil; because when (the Sun) comes to the world all sleeping mankind shall arise and awake. And the watchmen too shall cease from watching. The guards who sit at the gates of camps, they break vigil at the watchposts, because of its light that has shone upon them in the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the enumerative sequence (3/7). Uses human-nightwatch imagery as the natural expression of the day/night power shift, without institutional church markers.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth: It shall nourish, and give strength, taste and scent, to the trees and fruits and vegetables, and all the herbs, and the flowers and grasses, which are upon the entire earth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Correspondential register (‘strength, taste and scent’) and impersonal listing (4/7).

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth: When (the Sun) shines in all the world, the evil reptile and the sharp-toothed beasts that are filled of wickedness, they shall flee to hiding in their dens.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered list (5/7), presenting light’s dominion as a cosmic-natural deterrent.

paragraphs.core_text: The sixth: When it shines its light, the wound of any person is eased from pain. Its light shall melt away the evil arts of every doer of wickedness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered list (6/7) with light’s therapeutic/exorcistic efficacy expressed as natural effect; still expository rather than imperative.

paragraphs.core_text: The seventh: (The Sun) shall display and manifest to the world the sign of the splendour of the aeons of light, from which it has come out; it here in this world being their sign. It brings light to the whole of creation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Closes the sevenfold sequence (7/7) with explicit cosmos→cosmos signification (Sun as ‘sign’ of aeons of light).
Sect-polemic and evaluative address (‘foolishness… sects of error’) applying the teaching to opponents.
First-person instructional pivot (‘hear also what I teach you’) functioning as audience management rather than substrate exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: The first wickedness that the Night shall do in the world is the darkness, with which it shall fill the entire world; because when the sun sinks from the world and draws to it its rays, at that instant the shadow of the night shall spread out over the whole world. The eyes of the people fill with blackness. They neither see nor wonder with their eyes, because of the darkness of the night which shall fill the whole world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins a mirrored sevenfold negative sequence (1/7) describing the Night’s operations in impersonal, structured form.

paragraphs.core_text: The second evil thing that the Night shall do is its fear; because when its shadow looms forth, its fear and its trembling shall possess all of mankind. The entire world shall fill of the night.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered list (2/7) continuing the night/day correspondence as a mechanism.

paragraphs.core_text: The third: When the Night falls, all creatures take up revolt. They rebel in their heart, to do wickedness and perdition.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered list (3/7), still impersonal description of effects attributed to the Night as power.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth: The heaviness of sleep shall lay upon them, and they fall asleep; they slumber and doze, and they are like these corpses in the night.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered list (4/7), correspondential description (sleep/death-likeness) rather than exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth is its ugliness; again, when the Night would fall, the form of the people shall be hidden in the darkness and the ugliness of the night. The beauty and the form of men and women shall not be displayed before one another, because of its darkness and its ugliness, which it shall spread out over all their forms.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered list (5/7), aesthetic correspondence (beauty/ugliness) tied to light/dark mechanics.

paragraphs.core_text: The sixth occasion is when the Night would fall on the world. At that instant evil people shall come out to do wickedness; the adulterers, and the robbers and poisoners. The evil beasts shall come out, and all the reptiles that are filled with wickedness, from their dens. And they stalk in the night. Also, the demons and fiends find power to do wickedness in the night. Again, the blows and buffets and wounds and discharges shall torment people in the night; because in it the whole of evil shall find strength.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered list (6/7). Though it names social evils, it remains descriptive (what the Night empowers), not a direct prohibition or church rule; possible later moral coloring but presented as part of the fixed sevenfold schema.

paragraphs.core_text: The seventh: The Night shall display the sign of the Darkness, its father. It has arisen out of its essence; because this night that came out of this first Darkness has been displayed in the world. Note this night, the shadow of this first Darkness, the one that is entwined and bound in all things above and below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Closes the sevenfold night-series (7/7) with explicit dualist cosmology (Night as ‘sign’ of primal Darkness): cosmos→cosmos correspondence.
First-person summary plus sect-polemic (‘I have taught you… the sects have not seen…’)—application layer.

paragraphs.core_text: There are five archetypes occur in the Sun, it making them [...] as it finds the world.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the frame-like lead-in (“Once again he ramified. He says to his disciples:”) as editorial dialogue attribution; retained only the structural teaching claim announcing a fivefold schema.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying substrate is the fivefold archetype structure; the paragraph is introduced by a typical Kephalaia dialogue marker.

paragraphs.core_text: The first is its light; for it illumines by its light the world, and all the creatures who exist in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fivefold schema (1/5) stated impersonally.

paragraphs.core_text: The second is its beauty; because when it shines, it shall flood beauty and loveliness upon all creatures and everything.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fivefold schema (2/5), correspondential aesthetic register.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is its peace; for, again, when the sun would shine on the world, all people shall receive affection through it, and give peace to one another.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fivefold schema (3/5) presented as effect of the Sun’s appearing; still expository rather than imperative.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth is the life of the Living Soul, which it shall release from all the bonds and fetters of heaven and earth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fivefold schema (4/5) with explicit Manichaean cosmological entity (Living Soul) and liberation mechanism.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth: It gives a strength to the elements; and also it gives a scent and a taste to the entire Cross of the Light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fivefold schema (5/5) using correspondential registers (‘strength… scent… taste’) tied to cosmic structures (‘elements’, ‘Cross of the Light’).

Second-person address (‘you yourselves see’) and rhetorical superlatives comparing to ‘beauties of mankind’ and ‘powers and guards… in the world’; functions as homiletic amplification rather than structural mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, there are another three archetypes made apparent by the sun, in respect of the mystery of the first greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Introduces a threefold schema linked to the ‘mystery of the first greatness’; structural teaching move.

paragraphs.core_text: The first is the filling up of the disk of its ship; because its ship has filled up every season, and shall not wane at all, the way that the ship of the moon wanes. This continuous filling, by which it is filled, displays the mystery of the Father, the great greatness; from whom all the powers and the gods have come forth. He shall never wane, nor shall lack ever exist in him!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmos→cosmos correspondence: solar ‘ship’ fullness maps to the Father’s inexhaustibility; systematic analogy rather than citation or rule.

paragraphs.core_text: The second: (The sun's) light surpasses the light of all the stars, and all the lights that occur in the universe; corresponding to the mystery of the light of the Father; for his light surpasses and is greater than the light of his aeons.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Explicit correspondence formula (‘corresponding to the mystery…’) kept within cosmic degrees (Sun/stars ↔ Father/aeons).

paragraphs.core_text: The third: This sun is very high above all else. It surpasses the height of all the mountains and hills that exist upon the entire earth, corresponding to the mystery of the Father of Greatness; for he is high above all the household of his light-earth. Also, because the Father himself is high above all the heights and the mountains of his light-earth. He is 'filled up' in his image [all] the time and every hour from eternity to eternity!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third correspondence in a threefold set (height of Sun ↔ transcendence of Father of Greatness); strongly substrate-like, systematic and cosmological.
Direct address (‘O my beloved ones’) and sect-polemic; applies the mysteries to opponents rather than developing the system.

paragraphs.core_text: The mystery of the first great light is the sun, which is this second light-giver, the one that comes daily to the world. It displays all the marks of its graces, displaying and signifying on its own behalf that it is good, out of the essence of the good. It came from the good Father and appeared in this world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological identification of the Sun as ‘mystery/sign’ of the Good/Father; remains within cosmic ontology (origin/essence/sign).

paragraphs.core_text: In contrast, this Night that is made of fear exists after the mystery of the Darkness. Behold too the mystery of its essence! It displays it in the world in all these wickednesses. It displays this mystery daily in the world,
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the sectarian application (‘but the sects know it not… They do not distinguish…’) as editorial polemic applying the teaching to contemporary opponents.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens with a cosmos→cosmos contrast (Night ↔ Darkness) in the same ‘mystery/sign’ logic as the Sun section, then pivots into audience-facing polemic about ‘the sects’.
Explicit ‘the saviour’ allusion plus a Jesus saying (Thomas tradition); this material entered via Christian/Gospel overlay.
Apostolic speech tag plus NT/Pauline-style identity formula (‘children of the day/light… children of the night/darkness’), indicating Christian overlay rather than the oldest substrate.

Concluding beatitudes/blessings and soteriological exhortation (‘inherit life eternal!’) addressed to ‘my beloved ones’; functions as editorial homiletic close, even though it reiterates the two-essences doctrine.
